claims.statement: For uniform nonidentity P in G1 and uniform z in GT, input P and z, recover Q in G2 with e(P,Q)=z, the parallel Pollard-rho-in-GT algorithm in proof.md (one pairing to form g=e(P,Q0), P=4096 walks sharing one r=64 transition table with full-size uniform multipliers and starts and wrapping residues, dense Fp12 multiplications, shared distinguished-point table, G2 scalar mult, verification pairing) succeeds with probability at least 0.3995 using at most 2^127.65 total target-group-operation equivalents, including preprocessing and verification. Peak memory is at most 2^108.0 bytes; preprocessing is at most 2^24 target-group-operation equivalents and is included in total work; nonuniform advice is at most 2^0 bytes and is included in memory. This is a classical cold attack with no uncharged advice, quantum steps, or random-oracle premises. Success relies on the supported posited exploration law (pooled birthday with conservative merge factor, per-point labels, mixing degeneracy; no hash heuristic), the only heuristic, disclosed and supported in proof.md; degeneracy is a quantified (<= 1/r + 2^-100) heuristic event. This is an analytic best-known-attack cost analysis, not a claim of novelty or practical execution.

experiments.purpose: Run the identical multi-walk attack path in multiplicative notation on a fixed prime-order toy subgroup (n=9883) and measure success rate against the birthday prediction. This does not establish production behavior or cost bounds.

title: bls12-381-fixed-g1-invert-g2: parallel rho in GT, r=64, standard-regime wrapping walk, at 39%+ success
